title: Why We Forget Names and Remember Faces
meta_description: Learn why a familiar face can come with a missing name, how attention and memory retrieval interact, and which practical techniques help names stick.
author: Suraj Dahal
key_takeaways: Proper names can be difficult to retrieve because a person's name often has fewer meaningful semantic links than facts or descriptions associated with that person.
Recognizing a face and retrieving the matching name are different tasks; familiarity can be strong even when the name itself will not come to mind.
Attention during introduction, distraction, stress and weak encoding can make a name harder to remember later; a retrieval failure does not automatically mean the memory has been erased.
Repeating a name, linking it to a distinctive cue and retrieving it again after a delay can support learning, though no technique guarantees perfect recall.
